observations: Photo 0 shows two manual pallet jacks outdoors on grass.
Photo 1 shows a single manual pallet jack indoors on a tiled floor.
A '3.0T' capacity marking is visible on the pump housing of the red unit in photo 0.
A '3000kg' capacity marking is visible on the pump housing of the unit in photo 1.
No motorized forklift is visible in either photo.
The equipment shows significant signs of use, including paint loss, dirt, and surface rust on the forks.
The units are manual hydraulic jacks with standard twin-roller fork tips.

claims.evidence: No forklift is shown in the photos; only manual pallet jacks are visible.
Only 3.0T / 3000kg markings are visible; no other capacities are demonstrated.

risks.risk: Hydraulic pump failure or leaking seals preventing the jack from lifting or holding a load.
risks.proof: A video showing the jack lifting a full 3-ton load and holding it for 5 minutes without sinking.
risks.if_unproven: as having failed hydraulics requiring a full seal kit or pump replacement.

risks.risk: Seized or flat-spotted load rollers and steer wheels due to outdoor storage.
risks.proof: A video of the unit being pulled across a hard floor while loaded to ensure all wheels rotate freely.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring a complete set of replacement wheels and bearings.

risks.proof: A photo taken from the front at ground level to check the level and alignment of the forks.

proof_requests: Photos of the forklift mentioned in the description.
Video of the pallet jacks operating under load (lifting, holding, and rolling).
Clear photos of the manufacturer's data plates on the side of the frames.
Photos of any other units to verify the 'various tonnage' claim.
response.reason: The manual pallet trucks are clearly identifiable by type and capacity. While the forklift mentioned in the text is missing and cannot be priced, the pallet trucks can be valued based on their visible condition and 3-ton capacity, assuming a worst-case mechanical state until proven otherwise.
